title: NEC 2023 Articles 90–110 — Introduction, Definitions, and General Requirements
description: A 30-question practice test drawn from NEC 70, 2023 edition. The quiz follows the official 2-to-3 weighting with 12 questions on the Introduction and 18 questions on definitions and general electrical-installation requirements.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Code?
choices: To provide a complete design specification for every electrical installation
The practical safeguarding of persons and property from hazards arising from the use of electricity
To serve as an instruction manual for untrained persons
To ensure that every installation is efficient and adequate for future expansion
questions.answer: The practical safeguarding of persons and property from hazards arising from the use of electricity
questions.explanation: Correct: The practical safeguarding of persons and property from hazards arising from the use of electricity. Section 90.2(A) states this purpose and also states that the Code is not intended as a design specification or an instruction manual for untrained persons.

questions.question: What does compliance with the Code and proper maintenance provide?
choices: An installation that is essentially free from hazard but not necessarily efficient, convenient, or adequate for good service or future expansion
An installation guaranteed to remain adequate for all future electrical loads
An installation that requires no further inspection or maintenance
An installation optimized for the lowest construction cost
questions.answer: An installation that is essentially free from hazard but not necessarily efficient, convenient, or adequate for good service or future expansion
questions.explanation: Correct: An installation that is essentially free from hazard but not necessarily efficient, convenient, or adequate for good service or future expansion. This is the adequacy statement in 90.2(B).

questions.question: Which communications installation is outside the coverage of the Code?
choices: Customer-owned communications equipment installed in ordinary office space
Communications equipment under the exclusive control of a communications utility and located outdoors or in building spaces used exclusively for that installation
Communications cabling installed in a dwelling by the property owner
A premises network powered from customer-owned electrical equipment
questions.answer: Communications equipment under the exclusive control of a communications utility and located outdoors or in building spaces used exclusively for that installation
questions.explanation: Correct: Communications equipment under the exclusive control of a communications utility and located outdoors or in building spaces used exclusively for that installation. Section 90.2(D)(4) identifies this installation as not covered.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the general arrangement of the Code?
choices: Chapters 1 through 4 apply generally, while Chapters 5 through 7 address special occupancies, equipment, or conditions and may supplement or modify earlier requirements
Each chapter applies independently and can never modify another chapter
Only Chapters 1 and 2 apply generally; every later chapter is informational
Chapters 5 through 7 replace all requirements in Chapters 1 through 4
questions.answer: Chapters 1 through 4 apply generally, while Chapters 5 through 7 address special occupancies, equipment, or conditions and may supplement or modify earlier requirements
questions.explanation: Correct: Chapters 1 through 4 apply generally, while Chapters 5 through 7 address special occupancies, equipment, or conditions and may supplement or modify earlier requirements. Section 90.3 describes this arrangement.

questions.question: How do the requirements for communications systems relate to the requirements in Chapters 1 through 7?
choices: All requirements in Chapters 1 through 7 apply automatically
They are not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where a requirement is specifically referenced
Only Chapters 1 and 3 apply
Requirements in Chapters 1 through 7 can never apply
questions.answer: They are not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where a requirement is specifically referenced
questions.explanation: Correct: They are not subject to Chapters 1 through 7 except where a requirement is specifically referenced. Section 90.3 states this rule for Chapter 8 communications systems.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the status of the tables and informative annexes?
choices: The tables apply as referenced; informative annexes are included for information and are not Code requirements
All tables and informative annexes are mandatory in every installation
Tables are informational only, but informative annexes are enforceable
Neither the tables nor the informative annexes may be used
questions.answer: The tables apply as referenced; informative annexes are included for information and are not Code requirements
questions.explanation: Correct: The tables apply as referenced; informative annexes are included for information and are not Code requirements. Section 90.3 establishes the status of Chapter 9 tables and informative annexes.

questions.question: Who has responsibility for interpreting the rules, deciding whether equipment and materials are approved, and granting special permission where contemplated?
choices: The equipment manufacturer
The serving electric utility in every case
The authority having jurisdiction
The installer who obtained the permit
questions.answer: The authority having jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Correct: The authority having jurisdiction. Section 90.4(B) assigns the enforcing authority responsibility for interpretations, approval decisions, and special permission contemplated by the rules.

questions.question: When may a specific requirement be waived or an alternative method be permitted by special permission?
choices: Whenever the alternative costs less
When equivalent objectives can be achieved by establishing and maintaining effective safety
Whenever the installer has used the method before
Only when the serving utility requests the change
questions.answer: When equivalent objectives can be achieved by establishing and maintaining effective safety
questions.explanation: Correct: When equivalent objectives can be achieved by establishing and maintaining effective safety. Section 90.4(C) permits the authority having jurisdiction to waive specific requirements or permit alternative methods under that condition.

questions.question: Which words characterize a mandatory rule?
choices: Should or should not
May or may not
Shall or shall not
Can or cannot
questions.answer: Shall or shall not
questions.explanation: Correct: Shall or shall not. Section 90.5(A) states that mandatory rules identify actions specifically required or prohibited and are characterized by these terms.

questions.question: Which wording characterizes a permissive rule?
choices: Shall be permitted or shall not be required
Shall or shall not
Should be considered
Is recommended or is discouraged
questions.answer: Shall be permitted or shall not be required
questions.explanation: Correct: Shall be permitted or shall not be required. Section 90.5(B) uses these terms for actions that are allowed but not required, normally describing options or alternative methods.

questions.question: Are informational notes enforceable requirements?
choices: Yes, whenever they reference another standard
Yes, but only in commercial installations
No; they are informational only and are not enforceable requirements
No, unless the installer chooses to follow them
questions.answer: No; they are informational only and are not enforceable requirements
questions.explanation: Correct: No; they are informational only and are not enforceable requirements. Section 90.5(C) describes informational notes as explanatory material rather than enforceable Code requirements.

questions.question: How are SI and inch-pound measurements generally presented, and which value establishes compliance?
choices: Inch-pound units appear first, and both values must be met simultaneously
SI units appear first with inch-pound units immediately afterward in parentheses; compliance with either displayed system constitutes compliance
Only SI units may be used for compliance
Only inch-pound units may be used for compliance
questions.answer: SI units appear first with inch-pound units immediately afterward in parentheses; compliance with either displayed system constitutes compliance
questions.explanation: Correct: SI units appear first with inch-pound units immediately afterward in parentheses; compliance with either displayed system constitutes compliance. Sections 90.9(B) and 90.9(D) provide these rules.

questions.question: What does the term “approved” mean?
choices: Acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction
Manufactured in accordance with an ANSI standard
Listed by any testing laboratory
Accepted by the electrical contractor
questions.answer: Acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction
questions.explanation: Correct: Acceptable to the authority having jurisdiction. Article 100 defines Approved using this wording.

questions.question: What is ampacity?
choices: The maximum current, in amperes, that a conductor can carry continuously under the conditions of use without exceeding its temperature rating
The maximum fault current that a conductor can withstand for one cycle
The rating of the overcurrent device protecting a conductor
The current a conductor can carry without any adjustment for its installation conditions
questions.answer: The maximum current, in amperes, that a conductor can carry continuously under the conditions of use without exceeding its temperature rating
questions.explanation: Correct: The maximum current, in amperes, that a conductor can carry continuously under the conditions of use without exceeding its temperature rating. This is the Article 100 definition of Ampacity.

questions.question: Which conductors make up a branch circuit?
choices: The conductors between the serving utility and the service point
The conductors between the final overcurrent device protecting the circuit and the outlets
All conductors between the service equipment and a panelboard
Only the ungrounded conductors supplying a single appliance
questions.answer: The conductors between the final overcurrent device protecting the circuit and the outlets
questions.explanation: Correct: The conductors between the final overcurrent device protecting the circuit and the outlets. Article 100 defines Branch Circuit as the circuit conductors between those points.

questions.question: Which conductors make up a feeder?
choices: All circuit conductors between the service equipment, a separately derived-system source, or another power-supply source and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device
Only the conductors between a meter and the service disconnect
The conductors between the final overcurrent device and the outlets
Only conductors supplying motors from a motor-control center
questions.answer: All circuit conductors between the service equipment, a separately derived-system source, or another power-supply source and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device
questions.explanation: Correct: All circuit conductors between the service equipment, a separately derived-system source, or another power-supply source and the final branch-circuit overcurrent device. This is the Article 100 definition of Feeder.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: A continuous load is one for which the maximum current is expected to continue for ______ or more.
choices: 1 hour
2 hours
3 hours
8 hours
questions.answer: 3 hours
questions.explanation: Correct: 3 hours. Article 100 defines Continuous Load as a load where the maximum current is expected to continue for 3 hours or more.

questions.question: Which description meets the definition of a dwelling unit?
choices: A single unit providing complete and independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, cooking, and sanitation
Any sleeping room containing a bathroom
Any building occupied by one family, whether or not it has cooking facilities
A room providing temporary lodging and shared cooking facilities
questions.answer: A single unit providing complete and independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, cooking, and sanitation
questions.explanation: Correct: A single unit providing complete and independent living facilities for one or more persons, including permanent provisions for living, sleeping, cooking, and sanitation. This is the Article 100 definition of Dwelling Unit in the 2023 edition.

questions.question: What is an outlet?
choices: Only a receptacle installed for cord-and-plug-connected equipment
A point on the wiring system at which current is taken to supply utilization equipment
Any box in which conductors are spliced
A device that automatically opens a circuit during overcurrent
questions.answer: A point on the wiring system at which current is taken to supply utilization equipment
questions.explanation: Correct: A point on the wiring system at which current is taken to supply utilization equipment. This is the Article 100 definition of Outlet.

questions.question: When is one item of equipment considered to be within sight of another?
choices: When it is visible and not more than 50 feet distant
When it is in the same room, regardless of distance or visibility
When it is not more than 100 feet away and can be locked open
When its location is shown on a directory
questions.answer: When it is visible and not more than 50 feet distant
questions.explanation: Correct: When it is visible and not more than 50 feet distant. Article 100 defines In Sight From using a maximum distance of 15 m (50 ft) together with visibility.

questions.question: What is the service point?
choices: The point of connection between the serving utility’s facilities and the premises wiring
The load-side terminals of the service disconnect
The first outlet supplied by the service equipment
The grounding-electrode connection at the service
questions.answer: The point of connection between the serving utility’s facilities and the premises wiring
questions.explanation: Correct: The point of connection between the serving utility’s facilities and the premises wiring. This is the Article 100 definition of Service Point.

questions.question: How must equipment that is listed, labeled, or identified for a particular use be installed and used?
choices: In accordance with instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification
In any manner approved by the installer
Only in accordance with local utility preferences
Without regard to instructions if the equipment passes inspection
questions.answer: In accordance with instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification
questions.explanation: Correct: In accordance with instructions included in the listing, labeling, or identification. Section 110.3(B) establishes this installation-and-use requirement.

questions.question: In what manner must electrical equipment be installed?
choices: In a professional and skillful manner
In the least expensive manner that passes inspection
Only by using factory-assembled raceways
In a manner selected solely by the equipment owner
questions.answer: In a professional and skillful manner
questions.explanation: Correct: In a professional and skillful manner. Section 110.12 uses this wording for the mechanical execution of electrical work.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a required field-applied caution, warning, or danger marking?
choices: It must withstand the environment, warn effectively through words, colors, symbols, or a combination, and be permanently affixed rather than handwritten except for permitted variable portions
It may always be handwritten in pencil if it is legible
It is required to use words only and cannot use symbols or colors
It need remain legible only until the initial inspection
questions.answer: It must withstand the environment, warn effectively through words, colors, symbols, or a combination, and be permanently affixed rather than handwritten except for permitted variable portions
questions.explanation: Correct: It must withstand the environment, warn effectively through words, colors, symbols, or a combination, and be permanently affixed rather than handwritten except for permitted variable portions. Section 110.21(B) contains these field-applied hazard-marking requirements.

questions.question: What is required when a terminal is intended for more than one conductor or is used to connect aluminum?
choices: The terminal must be identified for that use
The conductors must be soldered to the terminal
A steel antioxidant compound must always be applied
The terminal must be installed only in service equipment
questions.answer: The terminal must be identified for that use
questions.explanation: Correct: The terminal must be identified for that use. Section 110.14(A) requires terminals for more than one conductor and terminals used to connect aluminum to be so identified.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a soldered conductor splice?
choices: It must first be mechanically and electrically secure without solder and then be soldered, with insulation equivalent to the conductor insulation or an identified insulating device
Solder alone may provide the mechanical connection if the joint is taped
It may remain uninsulated when enclosed in a metal box
It is prohibited for all premises wiring
questions.answer: It must first be mechanically and electrically secure without solder and then be soldered, with insulation equivalent to the conductor insulation or an identified insulating device
questions.explanation: Correct: It must first be mechanically and electrically secure without solder and then be soldered, with insulation equivalent to the conductor insulation or an identified insulating device. Section 110.14(B) states these splice requirements.

questions.question: Unless equipment is listed and marked otherwise, which conductor temperature basis applies to termination provisions for equipment rated 100 amperes or less or marked for conductors from 14 AWG through 1 AWG?
questions.explanation: Correct: 60°C. Section 110.14(C)(1)(a) generally bases these termination provisions on 60°C (140°F) conductor ampacity, subject to its listed-equipment and other stated allowances.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: For equipment operating at 0 to 150 volts to ground under Condition 1, the minimum depth of working space is ______.
choices: 2 feet 6 inches
3 feet
3 feet 6 inches
4 feet
questions.answer: 3 feet
questions.explanation: Correct: 3 feet. Table 110.26(A)(1) specifies 900 mm (3 ft) for nominal voltage to ground of 0–150 volts under Condition 1.

questions.question: What minimum width is required for working space in front of electrical equipment?
choices: The equipment width or 30 inches, whichever is greater, with space for at least a 90-degree opening of doors or hinged panels
Exactly 24 inches regardless of equipment width
The equipment width or 18 inches, whichever is less
36 inches measured from the center of the equipment
questions.answer: The equipment width or 30 inches, whichever is greater, with space for at least a 90-degree opening of doors or hinged panels
questions.explanation: Correct: The equipment width or 30 inches, whichever is greater, with space for at least a 90-degree opening of doors or hinged panels. Section 110.26(A)(2) establishes this width requirement.

questions.question: What space must generally be dedicated to an indoor panelboard installation?
choices: A space equal to the equipment width and depth, extending from the floor to 6 feet above the equipment or to the structural ceiling, whichever is lower, without foreign piping, ducts, or equipment in that zone
A 30-inch-wide space extending only to the top of the panelboard
A space extending 3 feet in every direction from the enclosure
Only the working space directly in front of the equipment
questions.answer: A space equal to the equipment width and depth, extending from the floor to 6 feet above the equipment or to the structural ceiling, whichever is lower, without foreign piping, ducts, or equipment in that zone
questions.explanation: Correct: A space equal to the equipment width and depth, extending from the floor to 6 feet above the equipment or to the structural ceiling, whichever is lower, without foreign piping, ducts, or equipment in that zone. Section 110.26(E)(1)(a) gives this indoor dedicated-electrical-space requirement.
